review_candidates.description: Forward-Deployed Engineer (Full-Stack + Unity) Customer-Facing Engineering, Bug Pipeline & Prod Support Future State University (FSU) About FSU We're building an AI-native applied learning platform: a 3D simulation engine that converts any syllabus or training doc into immersive, decision-based career simulations. Fortnite-meets-LinkedIn for education. Under the hood, FSU is a measurement system that happens to run as a game. Every decision a learner makes inside a sim becomes scored, traceable evidence of what they can actually do, and that evidence rolls up into the FSU Career Profile: a new kind of resume, built from behavior, not test scores. We are live in real classrooms right now, with real professors and real students depending on the platform on a real semester schedule. The Role We're hiring a Forward-Deployed Engineer to be the technical front line between our customers and our codebase. Today, support, triage, prod fixes, and professor onboarding get handled ad hoc by core engineering. That interrupts feature work and leaves no single person accountable for the customer's technical experience. This role consolidates all of it into one owner, spanning all three of our repos: the Unity simulation client, the platform backend (React/FastAPI), and the ML backend (Flask/Mongo). You will be on calls with professors and in the codebase the same afternoon. You reproduce the problem, pull the session data, decide what it actually is, fix it if it's yours to fix, and write a crisp ticket if it isn't. Then you close the loop with the customer: here's what happened, here's the fix, you're set. This is not a ticket-queue job. It's the role that turns customer pain into product signal, and it is one of the highest-leverage seats at the company because you see every failure mode before anyone else does. What You'll Own The bug pipeline, end to end. Single owner of intake, triage, resolution, and closure. Reproduce, classify severity, deduplicate, track status, keep reporters updated. Nothing goes silent. Triage and reproduction. Pull the relevant logs and session data and classify root cause before fixing or routing. This is the judgment step that determines everything downstream. Minor fixes across three repos. Small issues you fix directly, in Unity/C#, React/FastAPI, or Flask/Mongo. Anything deeper becomes a well-scoped ticket with repro steps, impact, and a proposed direction, routed to the right owner. Professor onboarding and course setup. Class configuration, roster issues, sim and course assignment, and the setup problems that aren't bugs but still block a customer. This is the bulk of real support volume. Prod data operations. Careful production data work: grade corrections, content and assignment changes, migrations. Backup first, always, inside the guardrails below. Post-deploy verification. Smoke test every release end to end, including launching a live sim, so breakage gets caught here and not by a professor mid-class. Proactive monitoring. Watch health and alerts for outages and degradations across memory, sessions, and third-party services, and raise them before they show up as customer reports. Runbooks and knowledge base. Turn recurring issues into docs and self-serve guides so the same problem doesn't get re-diagnosed five times, and so professors can resolve common things themselves. Voice of the customer. Spot patterns across bug reports and surface them to product and engineering as prioritized signal, with the underlying cause attached. What You Bring Strong communicator with real customer empathy. You're comfortable on a live call with a professor who is stressed, non-technical, and teaching in an hour. Excellent at reproduction and triage, and you write tickets other engineers are glad to receive. Confident in at least one of our stacks (Unity/C#, React/FastAPI, or Flask/Mongo) and comfortable reading the others. Comfortable querying data directly in Mongo or SQL. Startup-native. You operate without a playbook, you close loops without being asked, and you'd rather ship a fix today than design a process for next quarter. Judgment about scope. You know the difference between a fix and a change, and you don't quietly take on deep work that belongs with core engineering. Cross-stack fixing is a growth area, not a gate. We expect a new hire to fix confidently in one repo and triage well in the rest, and to build range from there. Bonus Unity or game-client experience, especially debugging builds in the hands of non-technical users. Forward-deployed, solutions engineering, or technical account management background. EdTech, LMS, or SIS integration experience (Canvas especially). You've built a support function from zero: intake, severity model, runbooks, the whole thing. How the Role Works We've built the guardrails in on purpose, so this role stays sustainable: Backup before any prod write. No exceptions. Deploy is commit-only. No unilateral prod deploys; the person who owns deploys ships. Escalate, don't improvise, on anything touching scoring, migrations, or billing. File a ticket, don't hand-fix. A bright line between "minor fix" and "file a ticket. How We'll Know It's Working Faster time-to-first-response and time-to-resolution. A healthy, deduplicated backlog with no silent threads. Fewer support interruptions to core engineering. Fewer post-deploy incidents that reach customers. Growing self-serve coverage. Professors telling us their issues get handled quickly and clearly. Why Join FSU You will be the person customers actually experience as FSU. You'll touch every layer of the stack, see every failure mode first, and have a direct line into what gets built next. Greenfield systems, real users on a real semester clock, high equity, real ownership, and a world-class mission-driven team. 🚀 See FSU in action: 🎮 Trailer: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H_i2L7BXH5A How to Apply Send your resume and a short note on the hardest customer-facing technical problem you've owned: what broke, how you found it, and how you closed the loop with the customer. Lawrence Bugg Founder & CEO, Future State University
